_readme: SAIRNlaw deadline engine -- holiday calendar extension, 2027 (amended) through 2031.
Phase 4 item 2. Loaded through add_holidays like every other calendar.
WHY THIS EXISTS: every jurisdiction carried 2026-2027 only, which was already
failing in production, not merely about to. A Pennsylvania matter triggered
2027-12-15 with a 60-day period crosses into 2028 and refused with
NOT_PROVISIONED -- verified live before this was built. The refusal was honest
and correct, but the coverage was going dark on 2028-01-01 regardless.
A REAL DEFECT IN THE PHASE 3 CALENDARS, found by the generator’s own
self-check rather than by a report: New Year’s Day 2028 falls on a Saturday,
so every both-way-shift jurisdiction (us-federal, in, mi, pa) observes it on
FRIDAY 2027-12-31. That date belongs to the 2027 calendar and was absent from
all four. Ohio is correctly unaffected -- O.R.C. 1.14 shifts Sunday only, so
its New Year’s Day 2028 stays on 2028-01-01, which is exactly the kind of
per-state divergence that would have been erased by generating one calendar
and copying it. The omission erred EARLY (a missing holiday means the engine
does not roll, producing a date earlier than the truth), which is the safe
direction, but it was real.
The 2027 rows here are the Phase 3 lists PLUS that one entry. They were not
regenerated -- those lists carry hand-verified reasoning in their authority
notes and re-deriving them would have discarded it.
Each jurisdiction’s shift rule is applied separately, never shared. The four
in this set genuinely differ, and that difference is load-bearing:
us-federal  Sat -> preceding Fri, Sun -> following Mon
oh          SUNDAY ONLY. No Saturday shift.
in          Sat -> preceding Fri, Sun -> following Mon
mi          five fixed days both ways; Christmas Eve / New Year’s Eve on a
FRIDAY shift BACKWARD to Thursday
pa          statutory dates do not shift; federal observed days added alongside
NOT EXTENDED, and deliberately so: Indiana municipal election days (vary by
locality), Pennsylvania county closure schedules (MCR-equivalent local
variance -- see that seed’s finding 5), and Michigan local administrative
orders. All three would require inventing facts about a specific court.

It was previously defined TWICE -- here and in the jurisdiction's own seed file -- with different content, so which one a licence held depended on the order the loader was handed its files and on nothing recorded in the repo. The seed copy has been removed; this is the only definition. 2027-12-31 IS a legal holiday here. New Year's Day 2028 falls on a SATURDAY and IC 1-1-9-1(b)'s two-way shift moves it back to Friday 2027-12-31, a date that belongs to the 2027 calendar rather than 2028. The removed seed copy already applied that same subsection in both directions -- Independence Day 2027 on a Sunday shifted to Monday 2027-07-05, Christmas Day 2027 on a Saturday shifted to Friday 2027-12-24 -- and omitted only this one, so the omission was an oversight and not a different reading of the statute. For FRCP purposes an Indiana holiday reaches only FORWARD-counted periods, per Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(6)(C). Good Friday 2027 computed as 2027-03-26 and confirmed against published calendars. NO election days are listed for 2027: Indiana's municipal elections fall in odd years and vary by locality, so they cannot be enumerated statewide from here -- an Indiana computation in 2027 landing near a local election day must be checked by hand. See the Indiana seed's _readme finding 4.

authority.citation: Mich. Ct. R. 8.110(D)(2) (holidays observed by state courts)
authority.note: SINGLE SOURCE for this jurisdiction's 2027 calendar as of 2026-08-29. It was previously defined TWICE -- here and in the jurisdiction's own seed file -- with different content, so which one a licence held depended on the order the loader was handed its files and on nothing recorded in the repo. The seed copy has been removed; this is the only definition. 2027-12-31 IS a legal holiday here, and Michigan is the subtle one. MCR 8.110(D)(2) shifts a Saturday holiday back to the preceding Friday, so New Year's Day 2028 (a SATURDAY) is observed Friday 2027-12-31. That sits alongside NEW YEAR'S EVE, which is itself a holiday here and which falls on Friday 2027-12-31 and therefore shifts BACKWARD to Thursday 2027-12-30. Two adjacent holidays, 12-30 and 12-31, is CORRECT and is not a duplicate -- it is the exact shape this calendar already carries for Christmas, where 12-23 is Christmas Eve observed and 12-24 is Christmas Day observed. The removed seed copy had the 12-23/12-24 pair and the 12-30 shift but not the 12-31 entry, which is what made it internally inconsistent. 2027 is the year Michigan's unusual rules actually fire, each checked by day-of-week: Juneteenth on a Saturday shifts back to Friday 2027-06-18; Independence Day on a Sunday shifts forward to Monday 2027-07-05; Christmas Day on a Saturday shifts back to Friday 2027-12-24; and Christmas Eve on a FRIDAY shifts BACKWARD to Thursday 2027-12-23, the rule with no analog anywhere else in this system. For FRCP purposes a Michigan holiday reaches only FORWARD-counted periods, per Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(6)(C).

authority.citation: Mich. Ct. R. 8.110(D)(2) (holidays observed by state courts)
authority.note: Generated 2026-08-22 from the statutory formulas verified against primary source in Phase 3, then re-checked by day-of-week -- the formulas are what was verified, so deriving dates from them is more faithful than transcribing a list. Per MCR 8.110(D)(2)(b): the five fixed days shift Saturday to Friday and Sunday to Monday, while Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve shift BACKWARD to Thursday when they fall on a Friday and to Friday when they fall on a weekend. No Columbus Day. This remains the MCR default -- MCR 8.110(D)(2)(c) authorises local administrative orders modifying it.

SINGLE SOURCE for this jurisdiction's 2027 calendar as of 2026-08-29. It was previously defined TWICE -- here and in the jurisdiction's own seed file -- with different content, so which one a licence held depended on the order the loader was handed its files and on nothing recorded in the repo. The seed copy has been removed; this is the only definition. THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO 2027-12-31 ENTRY HERE, and this note previously said the opposite. Ohio Rev. Code Sec. 1.14 does NOT shift a holiday that falls on a Saturday to the preceding Friday, unlike the federal rule in 5 U.S.C. 6103(b)(1) and unlike Indiana, Michigan and Pennsylvania. New Year's Day 2028 falls on a SATURDAY and is therefore not observed on Friday 2027-12-31 in Ohio. The same is true within 2027 itself: Juneteenth and Christmas both fall on a Saturday and are NOT shifted, which is why this calendar has no 2027-06-18 and no 2027-12-24 where the federal calendar has both. The generic amendment note this file carried until 2026-08-29 asserted that 'this jurisdiction observes it on FRIDAY 2027-12-31' for all five jurisdictions at once. For Ohio that was false, and it contradicted this entry's own date list -- the dates were right and the prose was wrong, which is the more dangerous way round because a reader checking the reasoning rather than the data would have 'corrected' the data to match. For FRCP purposes an Ohio holiday reaches only FORWARD-counted periods, per Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(6)(C).

authority.citation: 44 P.S. Sec. 11 (Pennsylvania legal holidays), together with the federal list, per Pa.R.J.A. 107(b)
authority.note: SINGLE SOURCE for this jurisdiction's 2027 calendar as of 2026-08-29. It was previously defined TWICE -- here and in the jurisdiction's own seed file -- with different content, so which one a licence held depended on the order the loader was handed its files and on nothing recorded in the repo. The seed copy has been removed; this is the only definition. 2027-12-31 IS a legal holiday here, by the FEDERAL half of the two-sovereign construction rather than the state half. Pa.R.J.A. 107(b) takes the federal list alongside 44 P.S. Sec. 11, New Year's Day 2028 falls on a SATURDAY, and 5 U.S.C. 6103(b)(1) makes the preceding Friday -- 2027-12-31 -- the federal observed day. It is labelled 'New Year's Day (federal observed)' for that reason. The statutory Pennsylvania New Year's Day is 2028-01-01 and belongs to the 2028 calendar, not this one. The removed seed copy already carried the identical pair for Christmas -- federal observed 2027-12-24 alongside statutory 2027-12-25 -- and omitted only this one. 2027 is the year the two-sovereign construction does the most work, each date checked by day-of-week: FLAG DAY falls on a Monday (2027-06-14) and is a real weekday holiday here, something no other calendar in this system can produce at all; Juneteenth on a Saturday brings federal observed Friday 2027-06-18 alongside statutory 2027-06-19; Independence Day on a Sunday brings federal observed Monday 2027-07-05. Good Friday computed as 2027-03-26 and confirmed. General Election Day computed from the statutory formula as 2027-11-02. Same deliberate exclusions as 2026 -- see the Pennsylvania seed's _readme finding 5. For FRCP purposes a Pennsylvania holiday reaches only FORWARD-counted periods, per Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(6)(C).

authority.note: SINGLE SOURCE for this jurisdiction's 2027 calendar as of 2026-08-29. It was previously defined TWICE -- here and in the jurisdiction's own seed file -- with different content, so which one a licence held depended on the order the loader was handed its files and on nothing recorded in the repo. The seed copy has been removed; this is the only definition. 2027-12-31 IS a legal holiday here. New Year's Day 2028 falls on a SATURDAY, and 5 U.S.C. 6103(b)(1) provides that 'instead of a holiday that occurs on a Saturday, the Friday immediately before is a legal public holiday', which makes Friday 2027-12-31 the day set aside by statute for observing New Year's Day -- the exact phrase Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(6)(A) uses to define a legal holiday. The date belongs to the 2027 calendar, not 2028: the engine resolves holidays by the year of the DATE, and the endpoint validator rejects a date whose year does not match its calendar, so filed under 2028 it would have been silently unreachable. THE DECIDING EVIDENCE IS THIS FILE'S OWN CONSISTENCY, not that it looks more complete: the removed seed copy already applied the SAME 6103(b) mechanism to Christmas -- 25 Dec 2027 is a Saturday and it carried 2027-12-24 'Christmas Day (observed)' -- while omitting the identical shift four weeks later. There is no reading of 6(a)(6) on which 12-24 is a legal holiday and 12-31 is not. STATED LIMIT: 6103(b)(1) is written for 'employees whose basic workweek is Monday through Friday' and for 5 U.S.C. 6309, not as a redesignation for all purposes. That scope clause is real and is not argued away here; the reading adopted is that 6(a)(6)(A)'s 'day set aside by statute for observing' points at 6103 as a whole, which is also the only reading consistent with the Christmas entry this system has been serving since 2026-08-21. Both-way shift per 6103(b): Saturday to the preceding Friday, Sunday to the following Monday. Every other 2027 entry is the Phase 3 list unchanged.
